answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-backed vouching. Each identity gets one vouch per epoch, valid only while its giver locks a bond slashed if two backed accounts prove to be one operator. Newcomers need vouches from the trusted core, so a puppet farm can only vouch for its clones and never enters it; it stays a plume outside the gate, the beacon of trust out of reach. That core is as rigid as quartz, so an attacker must bribe incumbents and cover their slashed bonds. Each fake identity then costs capital that earns no share, making mass registration a losing trade.
